title: SDK Gateway Prioritization: Enterprise Auth Patterns & Streaming Ergonomics Assessment
creator: Sofia Lin
description: Consolidate incoming enterprise requests for SDK/client libraries into a repeatable prioritization flow focused on two cross-cutting concerns: (1) enterprise authentication patterns (SSO/SAML/OIDC, token rotation, KMS-backed credentials) and (2) streaming ergonomics across polyglot clients (JS, Python, Java, Go). Deliver a short playbook and decision matrix that PMs + Eng + DX can use to triage requests, estimate effort, and recommend immediate mitigations (docs, patterns, short-term SDK adapters).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible intake checklist that captures security posture, auth topology, and customer constraints for each request
A prioritization matrix mapping customer size, security requirement, expected throughput, and streaming ergonomics risk to P0/P1/P2 decisions
Playbook doc with recommended short-term mitigations (adapter snippets, configuration flags) for at least 3 languages
Sign-off from Security and DX (Design/SDK owners) on guidance for token rotation and SSO patterns
A pilot triage run completed for 6 recent customer requests and updated priorities assigned
plan: 1) Collect and canonicalize 20 recent enterprise SDK requests from support, SE, and sales
2) Run 4 interviews with platform engineers and 3 enterprise customers to capture auth constraints and streaming pain points
3) Draft decision matrix and playbook; iterate with Security and SDK owners
4) Publish playbook in Confluence and share a one-pager for CS/SEs; create follow-up Linear tickets for implementable items
5) Do a pilot triage for backlog items and create implementation epics for top P0/P1 work
decisions: We will treat token-rotation + short-lived credentials as the default enterprise pattern unless customer mandates SSO-only (decision 2026-03-05)
For streaming ergonomics, prioritize SDK ergonomics for JS and Python first (most customer traffic and demo surface) and provide patterns for Java/Go as adapters (decision 2026-03-08)
Temporary server-side gateway adapters are acceptable as a medium-term mitigation to unblock customers while full client libraries are scoped
Security will require an explicit review for any flow that stores long-lived tokens on client machines
tradeoffs: Building full language-first streaming SDKs increases time-to-delivery (higher engineering cost) versus providing gateway adapters which are faster but add operational burden for customers
Standardizing on a single auth pattern (short-lived tokens + refresh) simplifies docs and SDK codepaths but may require SE to help customers who need SAML/IdP-specific integrations
Prioritizing JS/Python improves developer experience for a larger percentage of customers but defers enterprise JVM/Go-heavy customers who have stricter latency/throughput requirements
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial intake completed, 18 unique enterprise requests consolidated from Support, Sales, and Solutions Engineering
2026-03-04: Interviewed two platform engineers and one enterprise SE; captured pain areas around token rotation and reconnect logic for streaming in flaky networks
2026-03-05: Draft decision matrix v0.1 circulated to Security and SDK owners for comments
2026-03-08: Alignment meeting with SDK leads; decided to scope JS/Python ergonomics first and produce adapter examples for Java/Go
2026-03-10: Security provided initial feedback requiring KMS-backed credential recommendations for on-prem/private deployments
2026-03-12: Pilot triage run for 6 high-impact requests completed; created ENG-48210 and ENG-48211 for adapter prototypes and token rotation helper library
review_feedback: Security (Anika Rao): request more detail on threat model for refresh tokens; recommend default token TTL and rotation cadence
SDK Lead (Diego Marquez): favor small, well-documented helper libs over heavy SDK changes to avoid breaking existing consumers
Design (Maya Chen): ask that streaming examples include reconnect/resume UX patterns and a canonical error mapping table
Solutions Eng (Priya Nair): ask for offline migration guide for customers using older SDKs and for sample Nginx gateway config for token injection
notes: Follow-ups: create an SDK DX checklist item for token rotation in onboarding guides
If the pilot reveals more than 30% of requests require on-prem KMS integration, escalate to the Private deployment team for capacity planning
Consider a mid-sprint spike for ENG leads to prototype reconnect/resume semantics using the current streaming infra
